top.en: Your state decides your results. Rate it 0 to 10 and live at 8 or above.
top.zh: 你的狀態決定你的結果。為它打 0 到 10 分，至少活在 8 分。

top.en: Pain is real; suffering is a choice. Snap out of a low state fast.
top.zh: 痛是真的；受苦是選擇。要快速跳出低落的狀態。

top.en: Nobody triggers you but you. Thank the messenger who brings bad news.
top.zh: 除了你自己，沒人能觸發你。謝謝帶壞消息來的人。

top.en: Change is a decision in a moment, held by conditioning, not willpower.
top.zh: 改變是一瞬間的決定，靠制約維持，而不是意志力。

top.en: You don't need more information; you need stronger reasons.
top.zh: 你不需要更多資訊；你需要更強的理由。

top.en: Model people who already have what you want. Proximity is power.
top.zh: 模仿已經擁有你想要的東西的人。靠近就是力量。

top.en: Be an owner, not an operator: build systems and measure profit.
top.zh: 當擁有者，不要當經營者：建立系統，衡量利潤。

top.en: Success without fulfilment is failure. Celebrate more.
top.zh: 沒有滿足的成功就是失敗。多慶祝。

top.en: Energy is the base of everything: move, breathe, sleep, and never hit snooze.
top.zh: 能量是一切的基礎：動起來、呼吸、睡好，不要按貪睡。

title.en: Opening: the promise and the two worlds

lines.en: "You can get back your money, you can't get back your time." Tony frames the four days as a partnership: he over-delivers, you participate fully.
lines.zh: 「錢可以賺回來，時間回不來。」Tony 把這四天定位成一種合作：他全力超額付出，你全心投入參與。

lines.en: A trip is predictable and boring; a journey has adventure because you don't know what is next. This is meant to be a journey you "don't come back from".
lines.zh: 旅行（trip）可預期、無聊；旅程（journey）充滿冒險，因為你不知道下一步是什麼。這是一趟讓你「回不去」的旅程。

lines.en: AI, the economy and politics are the external world. You are more than anything that can happen to you. Two worlds to master: the external and the internal.
lines.zh: AI、經濟、政治是外在世界。你比任何可能發生在你身上的事都更強大。要掌握兩個世界：外在與內在。

lines.en: "Should" goals (I should work out, make more calls, spend time with my kids) only get done when easy. They have to become musts.
lines.zh: 「應該」的目標（我應該運動、應該多打電話、應該多陪孩子）只有在容易時才會做到。必須把它們變成「一定要」。

lines.en: Why all the jumping and clapping: moving, clapping and loud music raise testosterone and drop cortisol, and in that state you retain what you learn. "Results come by changing your biochemistry."
lines.zh: 為什麼要一直跳、一直拍手：動起來、拍手和大聲音樂會提升睪固酮、降低皮質醇，在這種狀態下學到的東西記得住。「結果來自改變你的生物化學。」

lines.en: Meaning drives emotion: in any interaction you decide "is this person challenging me, coaching me, loving me?" and the meaning you pick sets the feeling.
lines.zh: 意義決定情緒：在任何互動中，你都在判斷「這個人是在挑戰我、指導我，還是在愛我？」你選擇的意義決定了你的感受。

you.en: Treat the arena like a journey, not a trip: the staff feel your energy before they hear your words.
you.zh: 把競技場當成旅程而不是旅行：員工先感受到你的能量，才聽到你的話。

act.en: Turn one "should" this week into a "must" and write the reason beside it.
act.zh: 這週把一個「應該」變成「一定要」，並在旁邊寫下理由。

lines.en: Three focus patterns run your life: what you can control vs can't; past vs present vs future; what's there vs what's missing.
lines.zh: 三種焦點模式主導你的人生：能控制的 vs 不能控制的；過去 vs 現在 vs 未來；擁有的 vs 缺少的。

lines.en: Someone who focuses on what's missing, on what they can't control and on the past will be depressed, whatever drugs they take. Change the pattern and you change the feeling.
lines.zh: 一個人如果專注在缺少的、不能控制的和過去，不管吃什麼藥都會憂鬱。改變模式，就改變感受。

lines.en: Everything you do is for a feeling. You use "just enough logic to justify your emotional decision." Family really means love and connection; a billion dollars really means freedom or security.
lines.zh: 你做的每一件事都是為了一種感受。你只用「剛好足夠的邏輯來合理化你的情緒決定」。家庭真正代表的是愛與連結；十億美元真正代表的是自由或安全感。

lines.en: Every emotion you want, you have felt before, so it is already in your body. Your blueprint (your rules) is what keeps you from feeling it.
lines.zh: 你想要的每一種情緒，你都曾經感受過，所以它已經在你身體裡。阻止你感受到它的，是你的藍圖（你的規則）。

lines.en: Fear and faith are both imagination about a future nobody knows. Fear is imagination undirected (it grows like weeds); faith is imagination directed.
lines.zh: 恐懼和信心都是對沒人知道的未來的想像。恐懼是沒有方向的想像（會像雜草一樣長）；信心是有方向的想像。

lines.en: Darwin's real point: the most adaptable survive, not the strongest.
lines.zh: 達爾文真正的意思：存活下來的是最能適應的，不是最強的。

lines.en: Words change emotions ("nutritious vs delicious"; bum, butt and ass name the same thing and feel different). You cannot control the words other people use; you can change your reaction to them.
lines.zh: 用字會改變情緒（「營養的」vs「好吃的」；同一個部位用不同的詞，感覺完全不同）。你控制不了別人用什麼字，但你可以改變自己的反應。

you.en: When a staff member slips, the meaning you give it decides your mood and theirs.
you.zh: 員工出錯時，你給它的意義決定了你和他們的情緒。

act.en: Before reacting to a problem, ask: what can I control here, and what is already working?
act.zh: 對問題做出反應前先問：這裡我能控制什麼？什麼已經做得很好？

title.en: The future, three skills, and the seasons of life
title.zh: 未來、三項技能與人生的季節

lines.en: AI is moving tenfold in six months. Tony's advice: don't freeze in fear, get excited and "take advantage of it each step of the way". When life changes, you have to change.
lines.zh: AI 半年就進步十倍。Tony 的建議：不要被恐懼凍住，要興奮起來，「每一步都善用它」。人生改變時，你也必須改變。

lines.en: Three skills that remove long-term fear: pattern recognition, pattern utilization, and creation.
lines.zh: 消除長期恐懼的三項技能：辨識模式、運用模式、創造。

lines.en: Managing your life feels like stress; creating feels alive. Whatever your view of a creator, you were given the power to create.
lines.zh: 管理人生感覺像壓力；創造讓人覺得活著。不管你怎麼看待造物主，你都被賦予了創造的力量。

lines.en: Your life has seasons, and so does history. Stress comes from expecting every moment to be happy and perfect.
lines.zh: 人生有季節，歷史也有。壓力來自期待每一刻都快樂、完美。

lines.en: When times are good people think it will last forever; when bad, they think the same. Neither is true. "What always follows the dark night of the soul? The morning."
lines.zh: 順境時人以為會永遠順；逆境時也以為會永遠逆。兩者都不對。「靈魂的黑夜之後，接著來的永遠是什麼？早晨。」

lines.en: How long does real change take? Not six months, six weeks or six days. It happens in a moment, when you decide.
lines.zh: 真正的改變要多久？不是六個月、六週或六天。改變發生在一瞬間——在你下定決心的那一刻。

you.en: AI is changing your business fast; meet it with excitement, not fear.
you.zh: AI 正在快速改變你的生意；用興奮而不是恐懼去面對它。

act.en: Spot one pattern a week in the business (what sells, what breaks) and use it.
act.zh: 每週找出生意裡的一個模式（什麼賣得好、什麼常出問題）並善用它。

lines.en: "Relationship is 90% selection": you select who you are in your partner's presence, your best version or your burned-out one. The same two loving people are outstanding at peak energy, so-so when worn down, and fighting when burned out.
lines.zh: 「關係有 90% 是選擇」：你選擇在伴侶面前做哪個版本的自己——最好的版本，還是精疲力盡的版本。同樣兩個相愛的人，能量最高時非常好，疲累時普普通通，耗盡時就吵架。

lines.en: The law of familiarity: anything you are around enough, you start to take for granted.
lines.zh: 熟悉定律：任何你常接觸的東西，你都會開始視為理所當然。

lines.en: Energy is the single most important element of success. It does not come from food (Thanksgiving makes you sleepy; day three of a fast gives more energy) or from sleep alone. It comes from how you use your body and your breathing.
lines.zh: 能量是成功最重要的單一要素。它不只來自食物（感恩節大餐讓人想睡；斷食第三天反而更有精神）或睡眠，而是來自你怎麼使用身體和呼吸。

lines.en: Emotional muscles work like a bicep: the last hard rep builds it. Faith, courage and passion unused shrink.
lines.zh: 情緒肌肉就像二頭肌：最後最吃力的那一下才會練出肌肉。信心、勇氣、熱情不用就會萎縮。

lines.en: "You can't manage what you don't measure." The most important thing to measure is your own state, 0 to 10.
lines.zh: 「無法衡量就無法管理。」最需要衡量的是你自己的狀態，0 到 10 分。

you.en: Your energy at home and on the floor is a choice you make before you walk in.
you.zh: 你在家裡和場館裡的能量，是你走進門前就做的選擇。

act.en: Rate your state 0 to 10 before each shift, meeting and walk through the door at home.
act.zh: 每次上班、開會、回家進門前，為自己的狀態打 0 到 10 分。

title.en: How every emotion has a body pattern
title.zh: 每種情緒都有身體模式

lines.en: Live at 8, 9 or 10 as a minimum and push to 15. Most of the room admitted living at about a 6 since COVID. "Would you want a 6 leading your organization?"
lines.zh: 至少活在 8、9、10 分，並推到 15 分。現場大多數人承認疫情以來大約活在 6 分。「你會想讓一個 6 分的人來領導你的公司嗎？」

lines.en: Nobody made a sound until 7 or 8. Sound is one of the fastest ways to change your body.
lines.zh: 沒有人在 7、8 分之前會發出聲音。聲音是改變身體最快的方法之一。

lines.en: Incantation beats affirmation: words said with full body, face and voice change your biochemistry.
lines.zh: 「咒語」（incantation）勝過肯定語：用全身、表情和聲音說出來的話，會改變你的生物化學。

lines.en: "If I tell you something you forget it; if you discover it, you remember it." Then the five greetings exercise, which proved that annoyance, fear and joy each have the same body pattern in everyone.
lines.zh: 「我告訴你的你會忘記；你自己發現的你會記得。」接著做「五種打招呼」練習，證明煩躁、恐懼、喜悅在每個人身上都有一樣的身體模式。

lines.en: "Emotion is created by motion." "You don't need an excuse to feel good."
lines.zh: 「情緒來自動作。」「感覺好不需要理由。」

lines.en: Some emotions are brakes (fear, frustration, sadness, loneliness, anger) and some are accelerants (courage, passion, joy, determination, love).
lines.zh: 有些情緒是煞車（恐懼、挫折、悲傷、孤單、憤怒），有些是油門（勇氣、熱情、喜悅、決心、愛）。

you.en: A coach at a 6 runs a 6 party. Your team copies your body before your words.
you.zh: 6 分狀態的教練只能帶出 6 分的派對。團隊先模仿你的身體，再聽你的話。

act.en: Start the next team meeting with 30 seconds of movement and noise.
act.zh: 下次團隊會議用 30 秒的動作和聲音開場。

lines.en: Your blueprint is your beliefs, values and rules about how life, you and other people should be. Life matches it, you are happy; it doesn't, you aren't. Many rules are out of date.
lines.zh: 你的藍圖就是你對人生、自己和別人「應該怎樣」的信念、價值觀和規則。人生符合藍圖，你就快樂；不符合，你就不快樂。很多規則早已過時。

lines.en: Your emotional home is the small set of emotions you return to whatever happens. People in tornado country rebuild in the same spot because it's home.
lines.zh: 你的情緒之家，是不管發生什麼事你都會回去的那一小組情緒。住在龍捲風帶的人會在原地重建，因為那是家。

lines.en: The 9/11 story: Tony was running a seminar in Hawaii. Next morning, every person reverted to their home emotion: the angry stayed angry ("anger gets me things done"), the guilty felt guilty, the funny joked, the caring cared, the fearful thought it was the end times. "We only experience the part of life we focus on, and your focus is controlled by your emotional home."
lines.zh: 911 的故事：Tony 當時在夏威夷辦講座。隔天早上，每個人都回到自己的「情緒之家」：易怒的繼續生氣（「憤怒讓我把事情做完」），愧疚的覺得愧疚，搞笑的開玩笑，關心人的去關心，恐懼的人以為世界末日到了。「我們只體驗到我們專注的那部分人生，而你的焦點由你的情緒之家控制。」

lines.en: Most people regularly feel 12 to 20 emotions out of thousands that have names. Then the emotional home exercise.
lines.zh: 有名字的情緒有幾千種，大多數人經常感受到的只有 12 到 20 種。接著做「情緒之家」練習。

you.en: Under stress you go back to your emotional home; know which one it is.
you.zh: 壓力下你會回到自己的情緒之家；要知道那是哪一個。

act.en: Write your top 3 home emotions and pick one new one to practise this month.
act.zh: 寫下你最常回去的三種情緒，這個月挑一種新的來練習。

lines.en: "The quality of your life is the quality of your daily emotions." A billionaire who is angry every day has an angry life.
lines.zh: 「你的人生品質，就是你每天情緒的品質。」一個每天都在生氣的億萬富翁，過的是生氣的人生。

lines.en: Define the next level, not the ultimate dream: something exciting you could reach in 6 to 12 months if you focused.
lines.zh: 定義下一個層次，而不是終極夢想：一個專注的話 6 到 12 個月內能達到、讓你興奮的目標。

lines.en: "I overestimated what I could do in a year and underestimated what I could do in a decade." The early years are the momentum phase.
lines.zh: 「我高估了一年能做到的事，低估了十年能做到的事。」頭幾年是累積動能的階段。

lines.en: What has stopped you is always something inside: a belief, a habit or a habitual emotion. Decide what to let go of and what replaces it.
lines.zh: 阻止你的永遠是內在的東西：一個信念、一個習慣或一種慣性情緒。決定要放下什麼，用什麼取代它。

you.en: Pick the next level for the arena and gym, 6 to 12 months out, not the dream.
you.zh: 為競技場和健身房定下 6 到 12 個月的下一個層次，而不是夢想。

act.en: Write one sentence: in 12 months the business will be ___. Read it each Monday.
act.zh: 寫一句話：12 個月後生意會是 ___。每週一讀一次。

title.en: The science of achievement vs the art of fulfillment
title.zh: 成就的科學 vs 滿足的藝術

lines.en: Jim Rohn: "For things to get better, I had to get better." "Success leaves clues." Model people who already have what you want and you can turn nine years into nine months. Many people with "ten years of experience" have one year, ten times.
lines.zh: Jim Rohn：「要讓事情變好，我必須先變好。」「成功會留下線索。」模仿已經擁有你想要的東西的人，九年可以縮短成九個月。很多號稱「十年經驗」的人，其實是一年的經驗重複十次。

lines.en: Stop being a consumer, become an owner (every iPhone ever bought, about $22,000, vs the same money in Apple stock, about $240,000).
lines.zh: 別再當消費者，要當擁有者（買過的每一支 iPhone 約 $22,000，同樣的錢買蘋果股票約 $240,000）。

lines.en: Robin Williams mastered the science of achievement (his own show, number one in 18 countries, movies, an Oscar, money, family) and took his own life. "Success without fulfillment is the ultimate failure."
lines.zh: Robin Williams 精通了成就的科學（自己的節目、18 國第一、電影、奧斯卡、財富、家庭），卻結束了自己的生命。「沒有滿足的成功，是終極的失敗。」

lines.en: Find what fulfills you and give it to yourself, or you will judge others for having it. We don't celebrate enough.
lines.zh: 找出讓你滿足的東西並給自己，否則你會去批判擁有它的人。我們慶祝得太少了。

lines.en: Veterans segment: Born Primitive and Black Rifle Coffee paying down $100 million of veterans' medical debt; a veteran named Daniel told how a letter saying his debt was paid stopped him taking his life.
lines.zh: 退伍軍人單元：Born Primitive 和 Black Rifle Coffee 幫退伍軍人還清一億美元醫療債務；一位叫 Daniel 的退伍軍人分享，一封「你的債已還清」的信讓他放棄了輕生。

you.en: Model people already running what you want to run; it saves years.
you.zh: 模仿已經在做你想做的事的人，可以省下好幾年。

act.en: Name one operator to learn from and book one call with them.
act.zh: 找一位值得學習的經營者，約他通一次電話。

title.en: The one decision: live in a beautiful state
title.zh: 唯一的決定：活在美好的狀態

lines.en: Fulfillment needs two things: feeling that you are growing, and having more of yourself to give.
lines.zh: 滿足需要兩件事：感覺自己在成長，以及有更多的自己可以付出。

lines.en: Krishnaji (Oneness University) told Tony the most important thing he ever learned from him was changing state. A beautiful state is any state that lifts you. A low state you stay in is suffering.
lines.zh: Krishnaji（一體大學）告訴 Tony，從他身上學到最重要的一件事就是改變狀態。美好的狀態是任何能提升你的狀態；停留在低落狀態就是受苦。

lines.en: "Life is too short to suffer." Pain is real; suffering is a choice: it means staying in the bad state instead of snapping out.
lines.zh: 「人生太短，不值得受苦。」痛是真的；受苦是選擇——它代表你停留在壞狀態，而不是跳出來。

lines.en: "More rare than a billionaire: somebody who lives in a beautiful state when things don't go their way."
lines.zh: 「比億萬富翁更稀有的：在事情不如意時仍活在美好狀態的人。」

lines.en: With 121 companies and 5,000 staff, the chance someone is messing up right now is 100%. "If my happiness depends on you behaving a certain way, my happiness is pretty cheap," and it makes you a victim.
lines.zh: 擁有 121 家公司、5,000 名員工，此刻有人在出錯的機率是 100%。「如果我的快樂取決於你表現得怎樣，那我的快樂也太廉價了」，而且這會讓你變成受害者。

lines.en: The phone (checked 176 times a day) hooks you like a slot machine: the variable reward is what makes it addictive.
lines.zh: 手機（每天看 176 次）像吃角子老虎一樣勾住你：不確定的獎勵正是讓人上癮的原因。

lines.en: A real decision has three stages: decide, commit, resolve. Then the reasons-writing exercise.
lines.zh: 真正的決定有三個階段：決定、承諾、下定決心（resolve）。接著做「寫下理由」練習。

you.en: With many staff, someone is always messing up; your happiness cannot depend on it.
you.zh: 員工一多，總有人在出錯；你的快樂不能取決於這件事。

act.en: When something goes wrong, change your state first, then fix it.
act.zh: 事情出錯時，先改變狀態，再處理問題。

lines.en: Everyone will face extreme stress more than once. The question is what you do with it. "When you're going through hell, keep going." Its gifts: you find out who your real friends are, and you gain near-immunity to smaller stress (a friend who survived seven years as a POW: "After a North Vietnamese prison, what can the IRS do?").
lines.zh: 每個人都會不只一次面對極端壓力，問題是你怎麼處理它。「當你身處地獄，繼續走。」它的禮物：你會知道誰是真朋友，並且對較小的壓力幾乎免疫（一位當了七年戰俘的朋友：「在北越監獄待過之後，國稅局還能對我怎樣？」）。

lines.en: "Everybody's life becomes a story: an example or a warning." What puts you in a lousy state is thinking life should be different from how it is. Great stories follow the hero's journey (Wizard of Oz: ordinary world, the call, refusing it, the tornado, new allies and mentors).
lines.zh: 「每個人的人生都會變成一個故事：一個榜樣，或一個警告。」讓你陷入糟糕狀態的，是認為人生應該跟現在不一樣。偉大的故事都遵循英雄旅程（綠野仙蹤：平凡世界、召喚、拒絕、龍捲風、新的夥伴和導師）。

lines.en: "Who's doing the triggering? Nobody triggers you but you."
lines.zh: 「是誰在觸發你？除了你自己，沒有人能觸發你。」

lines.en: Business operator vs business owner: the operator does everything, makes every decision and is always stressed; the owner can be away for days and the business runs well.
lines.zh: 經營者 vs 擁有者：經營者什麼都自己做、每個決定都自己下、永遠壓力很大；擁有者可以離開好幾天，生意照樣運作良好。

lines.en: Tony's "killing the messenger" story: an employee lost $125,000 of a $500,000 business, Tony exploded, and that person never brought him bad news again, so problems got worse before he heard about them. He fixed it by interrupting his anger pattern.
lines.zh: Tony「殺掉傳信人」的故事：一位員工在 50 萬美元的生意裡虧了 12.5 萬，Tony 大發脾氣，結果那個人再也不敢帶壞消息給他，問題總是惡化了他才知道。他靠打斷自己的憤怒模式解決了這個問題。

lines.en: "Trade your expectations for appreciation and your whole life will change in that moment."
lines.zh: 「把期待換成感恩，你的整個人生會在那一刻改變。」

lines.en: HeartMath: in frustration the heart and brain rhythms are jagged and out of sync (the state where you crash cars and say things you can't take back). Two minutes of focusing on the heart with appreciation brings them into coherence: a flow state.
lines.zh: HeartMath：挫折時，心臟和大腦的節律雜亂、不同步（這就是會撞車、說出收不回的話的狀態）。專注在心臟、懷著感恩兩分鐘，就能讓它們同步：心流狀態。

you.en: If staff fear your reaction, bad news reaches you late.
you.zh: 如果員工怕你的反應，壞消息就會很晚才傳到你這裡。

act.en: Thank the next person who brings you bad news, before you respond to it.
act.zh: 下一個帶壞消息給你的人，先謝謝他，再回應內容。

title.en: Practical psychology: fear, the triad and the six needs
title.zh: 實用心理學：恐懼、三元組與六大需求

lines.en: The only thing that stops people is fear, and under every fear are two: I'm not enough, and so I won't be loved. Love is the oxygen of life.
lines.zh: 唯一阻止人的是恐懼，而所有恐懼底下都有兩個：我不夠好，所以我不會被愛。愛是生命的氧氣。

lines.en: Fear entered early: a baby is loved unconditionally while the mother's oxytocin is high; the first time she shouted or ignored you, you adapted to win love back. Some became achievers (praised for walking), some pleasers, some comedians, some got love by being hurt or having problems. "What's your childhood fight-or-flight pattern?" It may be overdone at 35 or 50.
lines.zh: 恐懼很早就出現了：嬰兒在母親催產素高的時候被無條件地愛著；她第一次對你吼或忽略你時，你就開始調整自己去贏回愛。有人變成成就者（因為會走路被稱讚），有人變成討好者，有人變成搞笑的人，有人靠受傷或出問題得到愛。「你童年的戰或逃模式是什麼？」到了 35 或 50 歲可能已經用過頭了。

lines.en: Don't fight fear (it pushes back) and don't give in (it takes you). Align with it: "Yes, I'm a little afraid, and let's try this instead."
lines.zh: 不要對抗恐懼（它會反推），也不要屈服（它會把你帶走）。與它同行：「對，我有點害怕，那我們換這樣試試看。」

lines.en: Your story ("it's not my fault, my childhood, my ADHD") is a wall that protects you from feeling not enough, and it imprisons you. Your body's cells are replaced every couple of years; the only way to keep an old upset is to replay the movie.
lines.zh: 你的故事（「不是我的錯、是我的童年、是我的過動症」）是一道牆，保護你不去感受「不夠好」，同時也把你關起來。身體細胞每幾年就全部換新；要保住舊的傷痛，唯一的方法就是一直重播那部電影。

lines.en: Only two things control the quality of your life: meaning and emotion. Three things control those: physiology, focus and language (the triad).
lines.zh: 只有兩件事控制你的人生品質：意義與情緒。而控制它們的是三件事：生理狀態、焦點、語言（三元組）。

lines.en: Why people do what they do: the six human needs.
lines.zh: 人為什麼做他們做的事：六大人類需求。

you.en: Staff and customers act from the six needs; meet the missing one.
you.zh: 員工和客人都是被六大需求推動的；去滿足他們缺少的那一個。

act.en: For one hard staff member, guess their top need and give them more of it this week.
act.zh: 針對一位難搞的員工，猜他最需要的是什麼，這週多給他一點。

title.en: State change and the fire walk

lines.en: A 35-minute guided rest ("about equal to three hours of sleep"), then a count from seven to one back to full energy.
lines.zh: 35 分鐘引導休息（「大約等於三小時睡眠」），再從七數到一，恢復滿滿的能量。

lines.en: The fire walk is a state-change drill: "If you can walk on fire, you can make cold calls easily." "If you feel scared, welcome to the fire."
lines.zh: 走火是改變狀態的練習：「如果你能走過火，打陌生電話就很容易。」「如果你覺得害怕，歡迎來到火堆。」

you.en: Fear is a feeling to walk through, like the fire.
you.zh: 恐懼是一種可以走過去的感覺，就像走火。

act.en: Do the call or conversation you have been putting off within 24 hours.
act.zh: 24 小時內打那通你一直拖著的電話，或進行那場談話。

lines.en: The telephone pole story: drivers hit the one pole on an empty road because they were staring at it. Look at the gap, not the pole.
lines.zh: 電線桿的故事：空曠的路上只有一根電線桿，駕駛還是撞上去，因為他們一直盯著它看。要看空隙，不要看電線桿。

lines.en: The lemon exercise: imagine biting a lemon and your mouth waters. Your body reacts to what you picture as if it were real.
lines.zh: 檸檬練習：想像咬一口檸檬，嘴巴就會流口水。你想像的東西，身體會當成真的來反應。

lines.en: So look where you want to go. Whatever you picture, eyes open or closed, your body works towards it.
lines.zh: 所以要看你想去的方向。不管睜眼還是閉眼，你腦中的畫面就是身體努力前往的地方。

you.en: Look at where you want the business to go, not at the pole you fear.
you.zh: 看向你想讓生意去的方向，而不是你害怕的那根電線桿。

act.en: Write the outcome first on every plan, before the problems.
act.zh: 每份計畫都先寫結果，再寫問題。

lines.en: Five steps: know your outcome, know your why, take massive action, notice what you are getting, change your approach.
lines.zh: 五個步驟：知道你要的結果、知道你的「為什麼」、採取大量行動、留意你得到的結果、調整方法。

lines.en: Jim Rohn: "Why comes first, how comes second."
lines.zh: Jim Rohn：「為什麼在先，怎麼做在後。」

lines.en: About 80% of New Year's resolutions are the same as the year before, because people check in once a year. Check in daily.
lines.zh: 大約 80% 的新年新希望跟前一年一模一樣，因為人們一年才檢查一次。要每天檢查。

lines.en: Sylvester Stallone story. He was turned down everywhere and sold his dog for $40. Watching Ali fight Chuck Wepner, he saw a man who kept getting up, and wrote Rocky in about 72 hours. He walked out twice when studios wanted the script without him in it. Later he paid $15,000 to buy the dog back, and the dog is in the movie.
lines.zh: 史特龍的故事：他到處被拒絕，把狗以 40 美元賣掉。看阿里對戰 Chuck Wepner 時，他看到一個一再站起來的人，大約 72 小時寫出《洛基》。片商想買劇本但不要他演，他兩次起身走人。後來他花了 15,000 美元把狗買回來，那隻狗也出現在電影裡。

lines.en: Simon Says game: "If you cheat here, you cheat at home." Afterwards: you only fail when you stop learning or quit. Only about 5% of the room decided "I'm going to win" before the game started. Reticular activating system (RAS). Neuroplasticity. We learn by repetition and by significant emotional events.
lines.zh: 「老師說」遊戲：「你在這裡作弊，回家也會作弊。」之後的結論：只有停止學習或放棄才算失敗。現場只有約 5% 的人在遊戲開始前就決定「我要贏」。網狀活化系統（RAS）。神經可塑性。我們透過重複和重大情緒事件來學習。

you.en: Check in daily, not yearly: the formula works only if you notice and adjust.
you.zh: 每天檢查，而不是一年一次：公式只有在你留意並調整時才有效。

act.en: End each day with one line: what worked, what to change tomorrow.
act.zh: 每天結束時寫一行：什麼有效、明天要改什麼。

title.en: Lasting change (McClendon, then a Tony video)
title.zh: 持久的改變（McClendon，接著是 Tony 的影片）

lines.en: Tony's story: he read 700 books in 7 years. After early success his ego grew, and he lost everything ("washing dishes in my bathtub"). The only two things that change us are pleasure and pain.
lines.zh: Tony 的故事：他七年讀了 700 本書。早期成功後自我膨脹，結果失去一切（「在浴缸裡洗碗」）。真正能改變我們的只有兩件事：快樂與痛苦。

lines.en: "If you're not doing it, you don't know it." Repetition is the mother of skill.
lines.zh: 「如果你沒在做，你就不算懂。」重複是技能之母。

lines.en: A psychiatrist attacked him on the radio. He did not attack back. He broke the pattern instead ("so you must be stating a hypothesis; a scientist tests it"), then cured a seven-year snake phobia in 15 minutes in front of 500 people.
lines.zh: 一位精神科醫師在電台上攻擊他。他沒有反擊，而是打破模式（「所以你是在提出一個假設；科學家會去驗證它」），接著在 500 人面前用 15 分鐘治好一個怕蛇七年的人。

lines.en: A man came back and said "you failed, you didn't program me right". Tony realised change is conditioning, not programming. Of 100 past clients, 96 held their change. The 4 who didn't all believed Tony had failed them.
lines.zh: 一位男士回來說「你失敗了，你沒有把我設定好」。Tony 領悟到改變是制約，而不是設定。100 位以前的客戶中，96 位維持住了改變；沒維持住的 4 位，全都認為是 Tony 讓他們失敗的。

lines.en: Three steps to lasting change: get leverage, interrupt the pattern, put a new pattern in its place and reinforce it.
lines.zh: 持久改變三步驟：取得槓桿、打斷舊模式、用新模式取代並強化它。

you.en: Change is conditioning: repeat the new habit until it is automatic.
you.zh: 改變是制約：重複新習慣直到它變成自動的。

act.en: Pick one habit and repeat it daily for 30 days with a reward each time.
act.zh: 挑一個習慣，每天做、做完給自己獎勵，連續 30 天。

lines.en: Human momentum = forward motion with emotion. Low energy breeds lower energy (the couch, scrolling on the toilet).
lines.zh: 人的動能 = 帶著情緒的前進。低能量會帶來更低的能量（沙發、坐在馬桶上滑手機）。

lines.en: Five steps: peak state, find your passion, decide/commit/resolve, consistent massive action, be SMART.
lines.zh: 五個步驟：巔峰狀態、找到熱情、決定／承諾／下定決心、持續的大量行動、目標要 SMART。

lines.en: McClendon posts on Instagram every day. He disliked it at first and enjoys it now.
lines.zh: McClendon 每天都發 Instagram。一開始很討厭，現在很享受。

lines.en: His phone-addiction story: he ran back downstairs, desperate for the toilet, to fetch his phone.
lines.zh: 他的手機成癮故事：明明很急著上廁所，還是跑回樓下去拿手機。

lines.en: Exercises: the happiness exercise with a partner, then the passion exercises done standing up.
lines.zh: 練習：跟夥伴做快樂練習，然後站著做熱情清單練習。

you.en: Momentum comes from small daily actions done with emotion.
you.zh: 動能來自每天帶著情緒做的小行動。

act.en: Do one visible daily action (a post, a call, a walk-through) for the next 30 days.
act.zh: 接下來 30 天每天做一個看得見的行動（一則貼文、一通電話、一次巡場）。

lines.en: Achievers are too hard on themselves.
lines.zh: 成就者對自己太嚴苛了。

lines.en: Parents praise a baby's first "mom", so the baby keeps trying. Praise yourself all of the time, not only when you win.
lines.zh: 寶寶第一次叫「媽」時，爸媽會大大稱讚，所以寶寶會一直試。要隨時稱讚自己，不是只有贏的時候。

lines.en: Self-praise moves: pat yourself on the back; the "Golden God / Golden Goddess" pose (Madonna's "Strike a Pose", standing like a trophy).
lines.zh: 稱讚自己的動作：拍拍自己的背；「黃金之神／黃金女神」姿勢（瑪丹娜的 "Strike a Pose"，像獎盃一樣站著）。

you.en: You are hard on yourself; praise is how anyone keeps trying.
you.zh: 你對自己太嚴苛；稱讚是讓人持續嘗試的方法。

act.en: After each attempt this week, praise yourself out loud, win or not.
act.zh: 這週每次嘗試後，不管成不成功，都大聲稱讚自己。

lines.en: Destiny is not far off. You are living today the result of decisions you made in the past.
lines.zh: 命運並不遙遠。你今天過的生活，就是你過去所做決定的結果。

lines.en: Pick one small decision and one hard decision, then embed each one with a ritual.
lines.zh: 選一個小決定和一個困難的決定，再用一個儀式把每個決定植入。

lines.en: Decide = cut off every other option ("burn the boats"). Commit = no matter what. Resolve = it is already done.
lines.zh: 決定 = 斬斷其他所有選項（「燒掉船」）。承諾 = 無論如何都做。下定決心 = 這件事已經完成了。

lines.en: Fourth step, gratitude: "Fear cannot exist when there's gratitude." Ended with singing loudly.
lines.zh: 第四步，感恩：「有感恩的地方，恐懼就無法存在。」最後全場大聲唱歌。

you.en: Today's arena is the result of past decisions; tomorrow's starts now.
you.zh: 今天的競技場是過去決定的結果；明天的從現在開始。

act.en: Make one hard decision this week and cut off the other options.
act.zh: 這週做一個困難的決定，並斬斷其他選項。

lines.en: Scott's mother went to the first UPW in Australia at 50 and came home with a 20-year plan. He was selling "caffeine and sugar" franchises with a beach house and a European car, and was not happy. He went to the next UPW unwillingly and made a decision on day 4 that changed his life.
lines.zh: Scott 的母親 50 歲時參加澳洲第一屆 UPW，回家時帶著一個 20 年計畫。他當時在賣「咖啡因加糖」的加盟店，有海邊別墅和歐洲車，但並不快樂。他不情願地參加了下一屆 UPW，在第四天做了一個改變他一生的決定。

lines.en: "Sometimes 10 seconds of bravery, 10 seconds of courage, 10 seconds of madness can change your whole life."
lines.zh: 「有時候 10 秒鐘的勇敢、10 秒鐘的勇氣、10 秒鐘的瘋狂，就能改變你的一生。」

lines.en: Tony is a "gap filler": he asks for the quickest, fastest, easiest way to close a gap. Someone has already closed it, so model them.
lines.zh: Tony 是一個「填補差距的人」：他會問怎樣最快、最簡單地補上一個差距。一定已經有人補上過了，那就模仿他們。

you.en: Someone has already closed the gap you face; find them.
you.zh: 一定有人已經補上你面對的差距；去找到他們。

act.en: Write your biggest gap and the name of one person who has closed it.
act.zh: 寫下你最大的差距，以及一位已經補上這個差距的人。

lines.en: Score seven areas of life from 0 to 10 and draw your Wheel of Life. A lopsided wheel at 100 mph is a bumpy ride.
lines.zh: 為人生七個領域各打 0 到 10 分，畫出你的人生之輪。一個歪斜的輪子用時速 100 英里在跑，一定很顛簸。

lines.en: Three Pillars of Progress: laser focus with strong reasons, a proven strategy, and resolving inner conflicts.
lines.zh: 進步的三大支柱：有強烈理由支撐的雷射般專注、經過驗證的策略、解決內在衝突。

lines.en: The gap map exercise. The Unleash app has the wheel.
lines.zh: 差距地圖練習。Unleash app 裡有人生之輪。

you.en: A lopsided wheel makes a bumpy ride, even at speed.
you.zh: 歪斜的輪子跑得再快也會顛簸。

act.en: Score the seven areas of your life this weekend and pick the lowest.
act.zh: 這個週末為人生七個領域打分，挑出最低的一項。

title.en: Why we don't do what we said (Scott)
title.zh: 為什麼我們沒做到自己說的事（Scott）

lines.en: We do things that meet three or four of our six human needs, and skip things that meet none.
lines.zh: 我們會去做能滿足六大需求中三、四個的事，跳過一個都滿足不了的事。

lines.en: Scott was 9.5 on health and 2 on money, and was tempted to work on health because it felt good. Pick the weak area.
lines.zh: Scott 的健康是 9.5 分、金錢是 2 分，卻很想繼續在健康上下功夫，因為那感覺很好。要挑最弱的領域。

you.en: You work on what feels good, not on what is weakest.
you.zh: 你會去做感覺好的事，而不是最弱的地方。

act.en: Spend 20 minutes a day this week on your lowest area only.
act.zh: 這週每天花 20 分鐘只做最弱的那個領域。

lines.en: The quality of your life is the quality of your relationships. "Even with AI, you're going to have to be in relationships with human beings."
lines.zh: 你的人生品質就是你人際關係的品質。「就算有 AI，你還是得跟人建立關係。」

lines.en: At the start, style matters more than substance. Match and mirror words, voice and body.
lines.zh: 一開始，風格比內容重要。配合並模仿對方的用字、聲音和肢體。

lines.en: First make people feel safe.
lines.zh: 先讓人感到安全。

lines.en: The A/B/C rapport exercise, demonstrated on stage (Rosanna and Catherine), then done by the room. Shares from Katie, Francois and Josie.
lines.zh: A/B/C 親和感練習，先在台上示範（Rosanna 和 Catherine），再全場一起做。Katie、Francois 和 Josie 上台分享。

lines.en: "Chosen family."
lines.zh: 「自己選擇的家人。」

you.en: Rapport sells parties and keeps staff: match first, lead after.
you.zh: 親和感能賣出派對、留住員工：先配合，再引導。

act.en: Teach coaches to match a customer's pace and tone in the first minute.
act.zh: 教教練在第一分鐘配合客人的節奏和語氣。

title.zh: 靠近就是力量（Tony 的影片）

lines.en: Peter Guber invited Tony into a group of about nine of the world's top people. Tony's first answer was "let me check my calendar".
lines.zh: Peter Guber 邀請 Tony 加入一個約九位世界頂尖人物的小圈子。Tony 的第一個回答是「讓我看看行事曆」。

lines.en: The richest man in Canada smacked down the newspaper Tony was hiding behind: "proximity is power."
lines.zh: 加拿大首富一把拍掉 Tony 用來躲的報紙：「靠近就是力量。」

lines.en: Tony went to New York every month for three years. Then came a deal worth $50M, then $400M. The dot-com crash took most of it.
lines.zh: Tony 連續三年每個月都去紐約。後來談成一筆 5,000 萬美元的生意，接著是 4 億美元。網路泡沫破滅時大部分都沒了。

lines.en: "We become who we spend time with."
lines.zh: 「你跟誰相處，就會變成誰。」

you.en: Who you spend time with decides who you become.
you.zh: 你跟誰相處，就會變成誰。

act.en: Book time this month with one person a level above you.
act.zh: 這個月約一位比你高一個層次的人見面。

lines.en: Everyone brings a gift. Find the people you lack (fun, financial maturity, emotional maturity). Platinum Partnership was trailed here.
lines.zh: 每個人都帶著一份禮物。去找你身邊缺少的人（有趣的、財務成熟的、情緒成熟的）。這裡預告了 Platinum Partnership。

you.en: Build a circle that has what you lack.
you.zh: 建立一個擁有你所缺少特質的圈子。

act.en: List what your circle lacks (fun, money sense, calm) and one person for each.
act.zh: 列出你的圈子缺少什麼（有趣、理財、沉穩），每項找一個人。

lines.en: SIPS. Spirit times money. Disappointment as an asset. Soul.
lines.zh: SIPS。精神乘以金錢。把失望當成資產。靈魂。

lines.en: Attracting luck (the TED muffins). The three Cs.
lines.zh: 吸引好運（TED 瑪芬的故事）。三個 C。

lines.en: Playing life on offense: a misogi and six mini adventures a year. "Last visit energy."
lines.zh: 用進攻的方式過人生：每年一個 misogi（極限挑戰）加六個小冒險。「最後一次拜訪的能量」（把每次見面都當成最後一次）。

lines.en: Rip up the playbook. "Never give your pain a voice" / "Outstanding". Ended with the story of his father and Billy Joel's "Piano Man".
lines.zh: 撕掉劇本。「永遠不要讓你的痛苦開口說話」／「Outstanding（棒極了）」。最後以他父親和 Billy Joel 的〈Piano Man〉的故事收尾。

you.en: Play life on offense: plan the adventures, don't wait for them.
you.zh: 用進攻的方式過人生：主動計畫冒險，不要等它來。

act.en: Put one big challenge and one small adventure on the calendar now.
act.zh: 現在就把一個大挑戰和一個小冒險排進行事曆。

lines.en: Halfway point of UPW. No backpacks tomorrow. Doors open at 8:15 and Tony is on stage all day: "come ready to leave some things behind."
lines.zh: UPW 過了一半。明天不准帶背包。8:15 開門，Tony 整天都在台上：「準備好放下一些東西。」

title.en: Day 1 and 2 review (Scott Harris, an Australian trainer who has been with Tony 30+ years)
title.zh: 第一、二天回顧（Scott Harris，跟著 Tony 三十多年的澳洲講師）

lines.en: Review on purpose. Tony reviews what he just taught every time he walks off stage. Do the same: call up what you learned instead of letting it fade, the way you forget a name a second after hearing it.
lines.zh: 刻意複習。 Tony 每次下台都會複習剛剛教的內容。你也要這樣做：主動回想學到的東西，不要讓它消失——就像聽到名字一秒後就忘記一樣。

lines.en: Energy first. Every Tony event opens with energy, because if getting out of bed is hard, everything else is hard. The jumping and dancing in the room exist to build energy, not for fun.
lines.zh: 能量優先。 Tony 每場活動都從能量開始，因為如果連起床都很難，其他事情都會很難。現場的跳躍和跳舞是為了建立能量，不是為了好玩。

lines.en: You are a creator, not a reactor. Your values, not your phone, should decide what you focus on. Every moment you choose three things: what to focus on, what it means, and what to do. Emotion usually makes the choice.
lines.zh: 你是創造者，不是反應者。 決定你專注在什麼的，應該是你的價值觀，而不是你的手機。每一刻你都在選擇三件事：專注什麼、它代表什麼意義、要做什麼。通常是情緒在幫你做選擇。

lines.en: "My pattern is not who I am, it's just who I've been." People, including kids, are not their behaviours. They run learned patterns, and patterns can change.
lines.zh: 「我的模式不是我，只是我過去的樣子。」 人（包括孩子）不等於他們的行為。他們在跑學來的模式，而模式是可以改變的。

lines.en: Two master skills: the science of achievement and the art of fulfillment. Achievement without fulfillment is failure. "A billion dollars and zero spirituality is zero."
lines.zh: 兩項關鍵技能：成就的科學與滿足的藝術。 沒有滿足的成就就是失敗。「十億美元加上零靈性，等於零。」

lines.en: Pain is only a short-term motivator. Achievers wait for the pain (the call not made, the invoice not paid) to become unbearable, then act, then ask "why didn't I do this sooner?" Run on pull (pleasure) instead: "I get to do this today."
lines.zh: 痛苦只是短期的動力。 成就者會等到痛苦（沒打的電話、沒收到的款）變得無法忍受才行動，然後問「我怎麼不早點做？」改用拉力（快樂）來推動自己：「我今天可以做這件事。」

lines.en: Recap of the six human needs, plus "people are only needy when their needs are not met." A leader's job is to find which one or two needs are missing for a customer, staff member or spouse and meet them. Listen first (two ears, one mouth); Tony always lets the person talk first so he can hear their map of the world.
lines.zh: 六大人類需求複習，加上「人只有在需求沒被滿足時才會顯得很需要」。領導者的工作，是找出客戶、員工或伴侶缺少的那一兩個需求並滿足它。先聆聽（兩隻耳朵、一張嘴）；Tony 總是先讓對方講，才能聽到對方的世界地圖。

lines.en: Momentum and NOW. The firewalk was easier than expected, and so are most calls, first videos and hard talks. "Never leave the site of a decision without taking an immediate action."
lines.zh: 動能與「現在」。 走火比想像中容易，大部分的電話、第一支影片、困難的談話也是。「離開做出決定的地方之前，一定要立刻採取行動。」

lines.en: Gap filler. Keep looking for the gap (I'm a 6, I want to be an 8) in health, money and relationships, and ask a peer group to point out the ones you can't see.
lines.zh: 填補差距。 在健康、金錢、關係上持續找出差距（我現在 6 分，我想要 8 分），並請同儕團體指出你自己看不到的差距。

lines.en: Less logistical, more intentional. In every coffee order, Uber ride and checkout, give the person your full attention for a few moments.
lines.zh: 少一點例行公事，多一點用心。 每次點咖啡、搭 Uber、結帳時，給對方幾秒鐘全心的注意力。

lines.en: "I work better under pressure" is a false belief. It's like telling a police officer "I drive better drunk." It works, but it exhausts you. Achieve from a beautiful state instead.
lines.zh: 「我在壓力下表現更好」是錯誤的信念。 這就像跟警察說「我喝醉開車開得更好」。它有用，但會讓你精疲力盡。要從美好的狀態去成就事情。

lines.en: "It's darkest right before the dawn." The most pressure often comes right before the breakthrough.
lines.zh: 「黎明前是最黑暗的。」 最大的壓力常常就出現在突破之前。

lines.en: The 2 millimetre stories: the plastic surgeon and Tony's golf lesson.
lines.zh: 兩毫米的故事： 整形外科醫師和 Tony 的高爾夫課。

lines.en: The training effect: full immersion, expert feedback, NET time. "When does the training end? Never."
lines.zh: 訓練效應： 完全沉浸、專家回饋、NET 時間（不需額外時間）。「訓練什麼時候結束？永遠不會。」

you.en: What you don't review, you forget.
you.zh: 沒有複習的東西就會忘記。

act.en: Review these notes for 5 minutes each Sunday.
act.zh: 每週日花 5 分鐘複習這些筆記。

lines.en: Tony gave everyone his book The Holy Grail of Investing (written with a partner whose firm, he said, made a profit on 96% of investments over 25 years). He takes no money from his four finance books; the proceeds feed people.
lines.zh: Tony 送每個人他的書《投資的聖杯》（與一位合夥人合著，他說對方的公司 25 年來 96% 的投資都獲利）。他的四本理財書都不拿任何收入，收益用來讓人有飯吃。

lines.en: He announced a partnership with The Agency (luxury real estate) and used it to segue into branding.
lines.zh: 他宣布與 The Agency（豪宅房地產）合作，並藉此轉到品牌的主題。

lines.en: Branding = identity. Coke lost most of the 1980s taste tests to Pepsi and still won, because of brand. Your brand is your beliefs about yourself.
lines.zh: 品牌 = 身分認同。 1980 年代的盲測中可口可樂大多輸給百事可樂，但還是贏了，靠的是品牌。你的品牌就是你對自己的信念。

lines.en: Identity shapes your mind and emotions more than anything. The limits are not what you can or cannot do; they are your beliefs about what you can or cannot do.
lines.zh: 身分認同比任何東西都更能塑造你的思想和情緒。 限制你的不是你能做或不能做什麼，而是你對自己能做或不能做什麼的信念。

lines.en: Today's plan: find your three most limiting beliefs and rip them out with the Dickens Process. Inner conflict drains energy, like a company that wastes its energy on internal fights instead of on the market.
lines.zh: 今天的計畫： 找出你最限制自己的三個信念，用狄更斯法把它們連根拔除。內在衝突會消耗能量，就像一家公司把力氣浪費在內鬥，而不是用在市場上。

lines.en: Your attention is being farmed. Companies make billions training people like lab rats to stay online and click; every click pays them.
lines.zh: 你的注意力正在被收割。 企業賺進數十億，靠的是把人訓練得像實驗室老鼠一樣一直上線、一直點擊；每一次點擊都在幫他們賺錢。

you.en: Your brand is what you believe about yourself, and the team feels it.
you.zh: 你的品牌就是你對自己的信念，團隊感受得到。

act.en: Write the three beliefs about yourself that hold you back most.
act.zh: 寫下最限制你的三個關於自己的信念。

title.en: The psychology of change, conditioning, values and rules
title.zh: 改變的心理學、制約、價值觀與規則

lines.en: Willpower has limits; conditioning does not. What looks like self-sabotage is usually mixed conditioning (pain and pleasure both linked to the same thing, like "marriage"), so you take two steps forward and one back.
lines.zh: 意志力有極限，制約沒有。 看起來像自我破壞的，通常是混合的制約（同一件事同時連結了痛苦和快樂，例如「婚姻」），所以你會前進兩步、後退一步。

lines.en: "Change is never a matter of ability, it's always a matter of motive." The mafia example: no one who "can't quit smoking" smokes with a gun to their family's head. You don't need more information about getting fit; you need stronger reasons.
lines.zh: 「改變從來不是能力的問題，永遠是動機的問題。」 黑手黨的例子：如果槍抵著家人的頭，沒有一個「戒不了菸」的人還會抽菸。你不需要更多關於健身的資訊，你需要更強的理由。

lines.en: Can you change someone who doesn't want to? Yes, with enough pain, but it has to be what they see as a must, not what you think.
lines.zh: 能改變一個不想改變的人嗎？可以，只要痛苦夠大，但必須是對方自己認為「一定要」，而不是你認為的。

lines.en: A Christmas Carol is the template. Scrooge had so much pain that his brain linked it to "being nice to people." He came to believe he was successful because he was mean, when really he was successful because he worked till midnight. The three ghosts showed him past, present and future so he had nowhere to escape to.
lines.zh: 《小氣財神》就是範本。 史古基痛苦到大腦把痛苦和「對人好」連在一起。他相信自己成功是因為刻薄，其實他成功是因為工作到半夜。三個鬼魂讓他看到過去、現在和未來，讓他無處可逃。

lines.en: How people dodge pain without changing: they shift the time frame ("it was fine before," "it'll get better"). Leaving a bad relationship finally happens when the brain says "painful in the past, painful now, worse in the future." The Dickens Process forces that.
lines.zh: 人們如何不改變卻躲開痛苦： 他們移動時間框架（「以前還好」「以後會變好」）。離開一段糟糕的關係，往往是在大腦說出「過去很痛、現在很痛、未來會更痛」的時候。狄更斯法就是要逼出這一點。

lines.en: Immersion beats drip-feeding, like learning a language: years of school classes versus 90 days in Rome. That's why the seminar runs with no meal breaks.
lines.zh: 沉浸勝過一點一滴地學， 就像學語言：在學校上好幾年的課 vs 在羅馬住 90 天。所以講座沒有用餐休息。

lines.en: Operator versus owner. At his first seminar Tony rented the Bonaventure Hotel in LA hoping for 500 people; seven showed up. Being self-employed means no leverage and constant cash stress. Now he owns 121 companies doing $22 billion. Ken Blanchard asked how he ran his business while travelling all the time. His answer: "Not very well. I only stayed in business because I added so much value."
lines.zh: 經營者 vs 擁有者。 Tony 第一場講座在洛杉磯租了 Bonaventure 飯店，期待 500 人；結果來了七個人。自僱代表沒有槓桿、現金壓力永遠很大。現在他擁有 121 家公司，年營收 220 億美元。Ken Blanchard 問他一直在旅行，公司怎麼經營。他的回答：「經營得不太好。我還能做下去，只是因為我創造了很多價值。」

lines.en: The embezzlement story. Tony split everything 50/50 with a partner. "Grow, grow, gone": revenue was booming but nothing was being measured. His accountant told him he was $758,000 in debt and the partner had fled to Mexico. Tony booked a flight to chase him. A friend told him the business would die while he chased revenge, and sent him to Fiji instead. There he realised he was angriest at himself ("anger is hurt at the highest level"). He kept asking "what really makes people do what they do?", woke up with the answer, filled three journals in one day, and built Destiny Technologies (later Date with Destiny). He came home calm for the first time because his values no longer conflicted. Lesson: get a CFO, even a virtual one.
lines.zh: 被侵占的故事。 Tony 跟一位合夥人什麼都五五分。「成長、成長、沒了」：營收大好，卻什麼都沒在衡量。會計師告訴他欠了 75.8 萬美元，合夥人已經逃到墨西哥。Tony 訂了機票要去追他。一位朋友告訴他，他去追仇的時候公司會死掉，叫他改去斐濟。在那裡他發現自己最氣的是自己（「憤怒是最高層次的受傷」）。他不斷問「到底是什麼讓人做他們做的事？」，醒來時找到了答案，一天寫滿三本日記，創立了 Destiny Technologies（後來的 Date with Destiny）。他第一次平靜地回家，因為他的價值觀不再互相衝突。教訓：一定要有財務長，即使是外包的也好。

lines.en: Every thought, emotion and action is controlled by two things: your beliefs and your values. That includes what you wear, where you sit, whether you came to this event, and whether you're married.
lines.zh: 每一個想法、情緒和行動都由兩件事控制：你的信念和你的價值觀。 包括你穿什麼、坐哪裡、有沒有來這場活動、有沒有結婚。

lines.en: Most beliefs and values are picked up, not chosen, by reacting against how you grew up or copying it. That leaves conflicts.
lines.zh: 大多數的信念和價值觀是撿來的，不是選來的——不是反抗自己的成長環境，就是複製它。這就留下了衝突。

lines.en: Values, rules and global beliefs: covered in the afternoon block.
lines.zh: 價值觀、規則與整體信念： 在下午的時段講解。

you.en: You don't need more information; you need stronger reasons.
you.zh: 你不需要更多資訊；你需要更強的理由。

act.en: For one thing you keep not doing, write 5 reasons it must happen now.
act.zh: 針對一件一直沒做的事，寫下 5 個現在一定要做的理由。

title.en: The Dickens Process, "I am the voice", gratitude
title.zh: 狄更斯法、「我就是那個聲音」、感恩

lines.en: The full Dickens Process exercise on the three limiting beliefs (steps under Exercises).
lines.zh: 針對三個限制性信念，完整做一次狄更斯法練習。

lines.en: The gang member story: a teenage girl whose best friend had just been shot said the voice in her head told her she wouldn't live to 30. Tony called her a follower for listening to it, then had her repeat the "I am the voice" lines with her whole body for 20 minutes and then 5 minutes twice a day. She left the gang, got three other girls out, and runs a small accounting business.
lines.zh: 幫派成員的故事：一個剛失去被槍殺的好朋友的少女說，她腦中的聲音告訴她活不過 30 歲。Tony 說她聽那個聲音的話，就是個跟隨者，接著要她用全身重複「我就是那個聲音」的句子 20 分鐘，之後每天兩次、每次 5 分鐘。她離開了幫派，還帶了另外三個女孩出來，現在經營一家小型會計事務所。

lines.en: A gratitude meditation: even the problems were grace; "life has always been happening for you, not to you."
lines.zh: 感恩冥想：就連問題也是恩典；「人生一直是在為你發生，而不是對你發生。」

you.en: Feel the full cost of an old belief and it loses its grip.
you.zh: 完整感受舊信念的代價，它就會鬆手。

act.en: Run the Dickens Process on one limiting belief this week.
act.zh: 這週對一個限制性信念做一次狄更斯法。

title.en: Scramble the old belief, install the new truth
title.zh: 打亂舊信念，植入新的真相

lines.en: Say the old belief like an idiot, interrupt it with the nose pattern, then replace it with the opposite truth and lock it in with rhythm and music.
lines.zh: 用很蠢的語氣說出舊信念，用「鼻子模式」打斷它，再用相反的真相取代，並用節奏和音樂鎖定。

lines.en: The three keys to lasting change were recapped.
lines.zh: 複習持久改變的三個關鍵。

lines.en: "Most people think forever and change their mind many times. Find your gut and go with it."
lines.zh: 「大多數人想個沒完，又改變主意好多次。找到你的直覺，跟著它走。」

you.en: An old belief said in a silly voice loses its power.
you.zh: 用很蠢的語氣說出舊信念，它就沒力量了。

act.en: Say the old belief in a cartoon voice, then the new truth out loud 10 times.
act.zh: 用卡通聲音說出舊信念，再大聲說新的真相 10 次。

lines.en: Tony said the crowd pushed back seven minutes longer than any audience ever had.
lines.zh: Tony 說這群觀眾比以往任何一場都多撐了七分鐘。

lines.en: "We judge ourselves too soon." As a young man in a 400 square foot bachelor apartment, he felt he had destroyed his life. The Neil Diamond song "I Am... I Said" was his turning point: "that's not how my story will end, this is the beginning of my story."
lines.zh: 「我們太早評斷自己了。」 年輕時他住在 400 平方英尺的單身公寓，覺得自己毀了人生。Neil Diamond 的歌〈I Am... I Said〉是他的轉捩點：「我的故事不會這樣結束，這是我故事的開始。」

lines.en: What's most important to you? The room shouted love, health, relationships, God, family, freedom, money. "If you organise your life around what's most important to you, your life will be unbelievably fulfilling. Most people forget, and let other things come in." He asked everyone to think about it over the one-hour dinner break.
lines.zh: 什麼對你最重要？ 全場大喊：愛、健康、關係、神、家庭、自由、金錢。「如果你圍繞著對你最重要的事來安排人生，你的人生會無比充實。大多數人會忘記，讓其他事情擠進來。」他請大家在一小時的晚餐休息時好好想一想。

lines.en: He introduced his wife Sage (transcribed as "Stacy").
lines.zh: 他介紹了他的妻子 Sage。

you.en: Organise your life around what matters most, or other things take its place.
you.zh: 圍繞最重要的事安排人生，否則別的東西會取而代之。

act.en: Write your top 3 values and check your calendar against them.
act.zh: 寫下你最重要的三個價值觀，拿來對照你的行事曆。

title.en: Energy, human excellence and the polo story (Tony)
title.zh: 能量、人類的卓越與馬球的故事（Tony）

lines.en: Energy is what he really wanted. At 23 he looked for the world's best endurance athlete and found Stu Mittleman, a social psychologist (not a natural runner) who ran a thousand miles at about 20 hours a day on 4 hours of sleep and beat the record by three days.
lines.zh: 他真正想要的是能量。 23 歲時他尋找世界上最強的耐力運動員，找到了 Stu Mittleman——一位社會心理學家（不是天生的跑者），以每天約跑 20 小時、只睡 4 小時跑完一千英里，比紀錄快了三天。

lines.en: Burn fat, not sugar. Stu studied a Central American tribe where every healthy person runs 76 miles once a year, as a celebration. They don't hit the wall because their bodies run on fat. "Fat burns like hot coals," for hours or days. Sugar burners spike and crash. Tony applied it and said it changed his life. (Detail promised for Day 4, health and vitality.)
lines.zh: 燃燒脂肪，不是糖。 Stu 研究了一個中美洲部落，每個健康的人每年都會跑 76 英里當作慶祝。他們不會撞牆，因為身體是靠脂肪運作。「脂肪燒起來像熱炭」，可以撐好幾個小時甚至好幾天。靠糖的人會暴衝又崩潰。Tony 照做後說這改變了他的人生。（細節留到第四天健康與活力。）

lines.en: Study outside your field (computer science, horticulture) to get new models.
lines.zh: 研究你領域以外的東西（電腦科學、園藝），才能得到新的模型。

lines.en: Schedule your growth in advance: book the places and times that will make you grow.
lines.zh: 提前安排你的成長： 預約那些會讓你成長的地方和時間。

lines.en: Disconnect to reconnect. At his Fiji resort he tells wired guests to put the phone away for a few hours: "Don't take 20 pictures of the waterfall. Experience the waterfall first."
lines.zh: 斷線才能重新連結。 在他斐濟的度假村，他會叫一直連線的客人把手機收起來幾小時：「不要對著瀑布拍 20 張照片，先好好體驗瀑布。」

lines.en: The polo story. A billionaire mentor who almost never gushes told him he must take up polo. A fan's letter the same week gifted five lessons. On a tiny horse called Ernie, during a "simulation," a real match thundered toward him, the ball landed next to him, and he scored. "I'm a polo player. Sign me up." Lessons from a good but not outstanding instructor were too slow ("I'll be 400 by the time I master this"), so he traded coaching with a nine-goal player (the top level) for three weeks of 5 am sessions. He learned in three days what took the master 20 years, and found an unexpected love of horses and sunrise. Two follow-up days a year (spaced repetition) made him the league's rookie of the year without having ridden before.
lines.zh: 馬球的故事。 一位幾乎從不熱情推薦東西的億萬富翁導師告訴他，一定要學馬球。同一週一位粉絲來信，送他五堂課。他騎著一匹叫 Ernie 的小馬做「模擬練習」時，一場真正的比賽朝他衝過來，球就落在他旁邊，他進球了。「我是馬球選手了，幫我報名。」一位不錯但不算頂尖的教練進度太慢（「等我學會都 400 歲了」），所以他用教練服務跟一位九分球員（最高等級）交換，連續三週早上 5 點上課。他三天學會了大師花 20 年學的東西，還意外愛上了馬和日出。之後每年再加兩天複習（間隔重複），讓他在之前從沒騎過馬的情況下拿到聯賽年度新人獎。

lines.en: Three keys to mastering anything: model someone outstanding, total immersion, spaced repetition.
lines.zh: 精通任何事的三個關鍵： 模仿頂尖的人、完全沉浸、間隔重複。

you.en: Energy is the product: steady fuel, movement, and time away from the phone.
you.zh: 能量才是真正的產品：穩定的燃料、運動，以及遠離手機的時間。

act.en: Model someone outstanding, immerse, then come back to it in a few months.
act.zh: 模仿頂尖的人、完全沉浸，幾個月後再回來複習。

title.zh: 第四天：健康、活力與行動

lines.en: Stop bringing your vision to people who are not visionaries. Avoid "unqualified proximity": people who have never been where you are going.
lines.zh: 別再把你的願景拿去給沒有遠見的人看。避開「不夠格的靠近」：那些從沒去過你要去的地方的人。

lines.en: His wife's glasses: "These are for me, not yours. You ain't supposed to see." Your vision is prescribed for you; others will not see it clearly.
lines.zh: 他太太的眼鏡：「這是我的度數，不是你的。你本來就看不清楚。」你的願景是為你配的度數，別人看不清楚很正常。

lines.en: People keep you in an old "file" and never update it. Some want the old you because the old you is useful to them.
lines.zh: 別人會把你留在舊的「檔案」裡，從不更新。有些人想要舊的你，因為舊的你對他們有用。

lines.en: Their level of support has nothing to do with your level of success.
lines.zh: 別人支持你的程度，跟你成功的程度無關。

lines.en: Consistency: you do not have a consistency problem; you are already consistent at the wrong things. You show up to a job you hate because you vividly know what happens if you do not.
lines.zh: 持續力：你沒有持續力的問題；你已經在錯的事情上非常持續了。你每天去上一份討厭的工作，是因為你非常清楚不去會發生什麼事。

lines.en: Success without fulfilment is emptiness. Do not become so successful at building a living that you fail at life.
lines.zh: 沒有滿足的成功是空虛。不要成功地賺到了生活，卻失敗地過了人生。

lines.en: Story: his mother died; 48 hours later his daughter was hit by a rock from a lawnmower; the scan found an early brain tumour. "That rock wasn't sent to break you, it was sent to build you."
lines.zh: 故事：他母親過世；48 小時後他女兒被割草機彈起的石頭打中；掃描時發現了早期腦瘤。「那顆石頭不是來擊垮你的，是來建造你的。」

you.en: Don't pitch your vision to people who have never been there.
you.zh: 不要把願景拿去給從沒去過那裡的人看。

act.en: Share big plans only with people who have built something similar.
act.zh: 大計畫只跟做過類似事情的人分享。

title.en: Dean Graziosi: putting it into action (business mastery forces)
title.zh: Dean Graziosi：付諸行動（企業精通的力量）

lines.en: Be the thermostat, not the thermometer. See opportunity, not obstacles; what you have, not what you lost; solutions, not problems.
lines.zh: 當恆溫器，不要當溫度計。看見機會而不是障礙；看見你擁有的而不是失去的；看見解決方法而不是問題。

lines.en: The next 12 months will bring more change than any 12 months in history; they can be 12 months to thrive.
lines.zh: 接下來 12 個月的變化會比歷史上任何 12 個月都大；這 12 個月可以是你大放異彩的 12 個月。

lines.en: Monday is coming: emails, doubters, the old life pulling you back. Plan for it now.
lines.zh: 星期一就要來了：一堆郵件、質疑你的人、舊生活把你拉回去。現在就先計畫好。

lines.en: Two shifts from Tony: life happens for you, not to you; and the fastest path is to find someone who has done it and model them.
lines.zh: Tony 的兩個轉念：人生是為你發生，不是對你發生；最快的路是找一個已經做到的人，模仿他。

lines.en: ROI, return on time, and COI: cost of inaction.
lines.zh: ROI：時間的回報；COI：不行動的代價。

lines.en: The monthly whiteboard exercise.
lines.zh: 每月白板練習。

lines.en: Force 2, creativity and innovation: innovation dies when you are alone and in your head. Who Moved My Cheese. Two restaurants in COVID: one blamed, one built a barbecue drive-through within a week.
lines.zh: 力量二，創意與創新：一個人關在自己腦袋裡，創新就會死掉。《誰搬走了我的乳酪》。疫情時的兩家餐廳：一家怪東怪西，另一家一週內就做出了烤肉得來速。

lines.en: Force 3, world-class marketing: fall in love with your clients, your product and their outcome. "If you build it, they will not come." 80 percent of books in a bookstore sell under 500 copies.
lines.zh: 力量三，世界級的行銷：愛上你的客戶、你的產品和他們得到的結果。「你蓋好了，他們也不會來。」書店裡 80% 的書賣不到 500 本。

lines.en: Force 4, sales mastery: money solves problems, sales bring money, so sales solve problems. Not marketing a great product is letting people suffer or buy from someone worse.
lines.zh: 力量四，銷售精通：錢能解決問題，銷售帶來錢，所以銷售能解決問題。有好產品卻不行銷，就是讓人繼續受苦，或去跟更差的人買。

you.en: Be the thermostat on Monday: set the temperature, don't read it.
you.zh: 星期一當恆溫器：去設定溫度，而不是只看溫度。

act.en: Write next Monday's plan tonight, including who will pull you back.
act.zh: 今晚就寫好下週一的計畫，包括誰會把你拉回舊樣子。

title.en: Joseph McClendon III: decisions, energy, breathing, water
title.zh: Joseph McClendon III：決定、能量、呼吸、水

lines.en: "Your destiny is shaped by the decisions you make today." Not deciding is a decision.
lines.zh: 「你的命運由你今天的決定塑造。」不做決定也是一種決定。

lines.en: Visualisation: picture a 73-year-old who made poor choices. Then he revealed he is 73, biologically 46 to 49, and has had no cold or flu in about 38 years.
lines.zh: 想像練習：想像一個 73 歲、做了很多糟糕選擇的人。然後他揭曉自己就是 73 歲，生理年齡 46 到 49 歲，大約 38 年沒感冒或得流感。

lines.en: "The snooze button is Satan." He wakes without an alarm.
lines.zh: 「貪睡按鈕是撒旦。」他不用鬧鐘也會自己醒。

lines.en: His mother was given three months; he refused the verdict ("I appreciate your diagnosis, but I will not accept your verdict"), used comedy videos and laughter, and she lived 11.5 more years.
lines.zh: 他母親被醫生判定只剩三個月；他拒絕這個判決（「我感謝你的診斷，但我不接受你的判決」），用喜劇影片和笑聲陪她，她又活了 11.5 年。

lines.en: Become the CEO of your own health. "What you write is what you invite."
lines.zh: 成為自己健康的執行長。「你寫下什麼，就邀請什麼。」

lines.en: Ten elements of health: six gifts to give yourself, four poisons to remove. Gift one is vital breathing, gift two living water and live foods (Dr. Batmanghelidj, "Your Body's Many Cries for Water").
lines.zh: 健康的十個要素：六份給自己的禮物、四種要移除的毒素。第一份禮物是生命的呼吸，第二份是活的水和活的食物（Batmanghelidj 醫師，《你的身體在為水哭泣》）。

you.en: Your health decides how long you can run the business.
you.zh: 你的健康決定你能經營生意多久。

act.en: No snooze button for 7 days; feet on the floor when the alarm goes.
act.zh: 7 天不按貪睡；鬧鐘一響就下床。

lines.en: People with real energy keep moving all the time. Every 30 to 40 minutes, get up and move.
lines.zh: 真正有能量的人一直在動。每 30 到 40 分鐘就起來動一動。

lines.en: Cells are like batteries; movement ignites them. When tired mid-day, move rather than nap or eat.
lines.zh: 細胞就像電池，運動會點燃它們。中午累的時候，起來動一動，而不是小睡或吃東西。

lines.en: "Our bones are strong with impact. Our muscles grow strong with resistance." 15 minutes a day of walking or rebounding matters.
lines.zh: 「骨骼因衝擊而強壯，肌肉因阻力而強壯。」每天 15 分鐘的走路或跳彈跳床就有差別。

lines.en: "Complexity is the enemy of execution." Billy Beck's free beginner, intermediate and advanced programme: billybeck.com/freetw.
lines.zh: 「複雜是執行的敵人。」Billy Beck 的免費初級、中級、高級課程：billybeck.com/freetw。

lines.en: Gift five: structural alignment.
lines.zh: 第五份禮物：結構對齊。

you.en: Movement is energy; sitting drains it.
you.zh: 運動就是能量；久坐會耗盡它。

act.en: Stand and move every 30 to 40 minutes at the desk.
act.zh: 坐在辦公桌時每 30 到 40 分鐘起來動一動。

title.en: Structural alignment coach: posture, coaching with love, biomechanics
title.zh: 結構對齊教練：姿勢、用愛指導、生物力學

lines.en: Walk into a room like you own it.
lines.zh: 走進一個房間時，要像那是你的地盤。

lines.en: Coaching with love: telling a kid "change it, you're a screw up" makes him fight back. Lead with "I love you no matter what, and I want more for you," then give the instruction.
lines.zh: 用愛指導：對孩子說「改掉，你這個搞砸的傢伙」只會讓他反抗。先說「不管怎樣我都愛你，我希望你更好」，再給指令。

lines.en: Bunions are a callus from the foot turning out and rolling off the inside; fix the gait, not the bunion.
lines.zh: 拇趾外翻是腳往外轉、從內側滾出去造成的繭；要修正的是步態，不是拇趾外翻本身。

lines.en: A fast athlete with a lopsided frame gets injured three games in. Alignment is a business risk.
lines.zh: 一個速度很快但骨架歪斜的運動員，打三場就會受傷。對齊是一種經營風險。

lines.en: Upper back and neck position may affect fluid drainage from the head.
lines.zh: 上背和頸部的位置可能會影響頭部的體液引流。

lines.en: Kids: watch for knees caving in ("that's an ACL in the making"). Balanced, bilateral bodies move better.
lines.zh: 孩子：注意膝蓋往內塌（「那是十字韌帶受傷的前兆」）。左右平衡的身體動得更好。

lines.en: "This is not a flexibility issue. Stop stretching, unless you're going after the reason you're tight, which is your frame is off."
lines.zh: 「這不是柔軟度的問題。別再拉筋了，除非你要處理的是緊繃的原因：你的骨架歪了。」

lines.en: Live routine on stage (see Exercises).
lines.zh: 台上現場示範一套對齊動作。

lines.en: Joseph after: placebo studies, "your body is a pharmacy", focus equals feeling, heart breathing with gratitude, praise yourself to condition the habit.
lines.zh: 之後 Joseph 接著講：安慰劑研究、「你的身體就是一間藥房」、焦點等於感受、帶著感恩做心臟呼吸、稱讚自己來制約習慣。

you.en: Coach with love first, then correct: it applies to staff and kids.
you.zh: 先用愛指導，再糾正：對員工和孩子都一樣。

act.en: Open your next correction with: I want more for you.
act.zh: 下一次糾正別人時，用「我希望你更好」開頭。

title.en: Dr. Dawn Mussallem (Fountain Life): longevity basics
title.zh: Dawn Mussallem 醫師（Fountain Life）：長壽的基本

lines.en: "Being alive and feeling alive are two separate things. The second one is a choice." "Fear and gratitude can't live together."
lines.zh: 「活著和覺得活著是兩回事。第二個是選擇。」「恐懼和感恩無法同時存在。」

lines.en: 88 percent of otherwise healthy people screened had cardiac plaque; 50 percent of heart attacks have no symptoms.
lines.zh: 接受檢查的健康人中，88% 有心臟斑塊；50% 的心臟病發作沒有任何症狀。

lines.en: Food as medicine: half of every plate vegetables and fruit. Avoid ultra-processed food, processed meat, sugary drinks; read labels.
lines.zh: 食物就是藥：每一盤有一半是蔬菜和水果。避免超加工食品、加工肉品、含糖飲料；要看標籤。

lines.en: Fibre is forgotten (95 percent deficient). Plant protein (beans) did best for healthy ageing.
lines.zh: 纖維被遺忘了（95% 的人攝取不足）。植物性蛋白質（豆類）對健康老化最有幫助。

lines.en: Steps: benefit starts around 7,000. Add three one-minute fast bursts a day. Resistance 30 to 60 minutes a week minimum, 90 to 120 better; combine with cardio. Do not sit more than about 10.6 hours; move every 20 to 30 minutes; walk after meals.
lines.zh: 步數：大約 7,000 步開始有效益。每天加三次一分鐘的快速爆發。阻力訓練每週至少 30 到 60 分鐘，90 到 120 分鐘更好；搭配有氧。每天久坐不要超過約 10.6 小時；每 20 到 30 分鐘動一下；飯後散步。

lines.en: Sleep regularity matters most: same wake time daily, morning light.
lines.zh: 睡眠的規律最重要：每天同一時間起床、早上照到光。

lines.en: Optimism and relationships predict healthy ageing more than cholesterol. Volunteering two hours a week helps.
lines.zh: 樂觀和人際關係比膽固醇更能預測健康老化。每週當兩小時志工有幫助。

lines.en: The heart keeps 5 percent of the blood for itself and gives 95 percent away.
lines.zh: 心臟只留 5% 的血液給自己，把 95% 送出去。

you.en: Long life is built from steps, sleep, fibre and people.
you.zh: 長壽來自步數、睡眠、纖維和人際關係。

act.en: Walk 7,000 steps and after meals for 7 days; same wake time daily.
act.zh: 連續 7 天每天走 7,000 步、飯後散步，每天同一時間起床。

lines.en: Built SBE (100 hotels, 150 restaurants), sold four months before COVID at 44, in his least healthy state. Read Life Force, got an intro to Tony via A.J. Gupta, and partnered on longevity residences.
lines.zh: 創立 SBE（100 家飯店、150 家餐廳），44 歲時在疫情前四個月賣掉，當時是他最不健康的時候。讀了《Life Force》，透過 A.J. Gupta 認識 Tony，合作打造長壽住宅。

steps.en: Ask: where am I, 0 to 10?
steps.zh: 問自己：我現在 0 到 10 分是幾分？

steps.en: If under 8, move: stand, breathe hard, make a sound.
steps.zh: 低於 8 分就動起來：站起來、用力呼吸、發出聲音。

steps.en: Do it before every shift, meeting and walking in at home.
steps.zh: 每次上班、開會、回家進門前都做。

steps.en: Put your attention on your heart, hand on chest if it helps.
steps.zh: 把注意力放在心臟上，可以把手放在胸口。

steps.en: Breathe slowly, about 5 seconds in and 5 out.
steps.zh: 慢慢呼吸，大約吸 5 秒、吐 5 秒。

steps.en: Feel thanks for one specific thing, then think about the stressful task.
steps.zh: 對一件具體的事心懷感謝，再去想那件有壓力的事。

steps.en: List the emotions you feel most weeks, good and bad.
steps.zh: 列出你大多數週都會有的情緒，好的壞的都寫。

steps.en: Circle the 3 you return to under stress.
steps.zh: 圈出壓力下最常回去的 3 種。

steps.en: Pick one empowering emotion to practise daily for a month.
steps.zh: 挑一種有力量的情緒，每天練習一個月。

steps.en: Write one limiting belief.
steps.zh: 寫下一個限制性信念。

steps.en: Ask what it has cost you in the past: health, money, people. Feel it.
steps.zh: 問它過去讓你付出了什麼代價：健康、金錢、人際。去感受它。

steps.en: Ask what it costs you now, then 5, 10 and 20 years from now if nothing changes.
steps.zh: 問它現在讓你付出什麼，以及如果不改變，5、10、20 年後會怎樣。

steps.en: Shake it off, then picture the same years living the opposite belief.
steps.zh: 甩掉它，再想像同樣的年份，活在相反的信念裡。

steps.en: Write the new belief and say it out loud with your whole body.
steps.zh: 寫下新的信念，用全身大聲說出來。

steps.en: Write one decision and cross out every other option.
steps.zh: 寫下一個決定，劃掉其他所有選項。

steps.en: Write why it must happen, at least 5 reasons.
steps.zh: 寫下為什麼一定要做，至少 5 個理由。

steps.en: Take one action on it before you leave the room.
steps.zh: 離開房間前就為它採取一個行動。

steps.en: Finish with gratitude: name 3 things you are thankful for.
steps.zh: 以感恩結束：說出 3 件你感謝的事。

title.en: Wheel of life and gap map

steps.en: Score 7 areas 0 to 10: health, emotions, relationships, time, career, money, contribution.
steps.zh: 為 7 個領域打 0 到 10 分：健康、情緒、關係、時間、事業、金錢、貢獻。

steps.en: Pick the lowest area.
steps.zh: 挑出最低的領域。

steps.en: Write where you are and why, where you want to be and why, the tools you need and what is in the way.
steps.zh: 寫下現在在哪裡和原因、想去哪裡和原因、需要的工具，以及擋路的是什麼。

steps.en: Redo it every quarter.
steps.zh: 每季重做一次。

steps.en: Feet on the floor at the alarm, no snooze, bright light in your eyes.
steps.zh: 鬧鐘一響就下床，不按貪睡，讓眼睛照到亮光。

steps.en: Say: this is a great day because I get to ___.
steps.zh: 說：今天是很棒的一天，因為我可以 ___。

steps.en: Name what you want today, then 2 minutes of heart breathing.
steps.zh: 說出今天想要的結果，再做 2 分鐘心臟呼吸。

steps.en: After any attempt, win or lose, pat yourself on the back and say "good job".
steps.zh: 任何一次嘗試後，不管輸贏，拍拍自己的背說「做得好」。

steps.en: Do it out loud; the brain learns from celebration.
steps.zh: 要大聲說；大腦是從慶祝中學習的。

note.en: From Sam's recordings of the event. Stage lines are paraphrased where the audio was unclear.
note.zh: 來自 Sam 在現場的錄音。錄音不清楚的地方，台上的話以意譯呈現。
